blindSummary:
On 10 October 2022 the student-affairs office of a state university in this state/province told students perceived as trans women that they would be barred from university premises unless they cut their hair and wore the uniform prescribed for males, delivering the instruction through campus guards with one week to comply and threatening that they could not re-enrol otherwise; the office attributed the order to the university president. A legal-aid organisation's case study documents the students' subsequent advocacy campaign - backed by paralegals of national LGBTQ organisations, who pointed to an existing municipal anti-discrimination ordinance in the town where the campus sits, which the office dismissed as inapplicable - and its later milestone: the first openly trans woman graduating as university valedictorian with highest honours. This is a documented episode of institutional gender-expression policing in a conservative, non-metropolitan setting, reversed by advocacy.

No killings from the 2024-2025 national series occurred in this state/province. The campus directive is a resident-facing action rather than a mechanism a visitor encounters; its force as a regional signal is that in a conservative, non-metropolitan setting expression can be policed by institutional authority without local recourse operating - and unlike a neighbouring state/province, this state/province has no protective-ordinance cluster of comparable reach.
